facts.fact: Agent Bricks is now the umbrella name for Databricks' agent developer platform (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/concepts/ ; https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/generative-ai/agent-framework/build-genai-apps)

The Agent Bricks overview lists its components as Agent Bricks CLI, Agent Runtime, the DurableAgentServer agent server, Databricks Sandbox, Unity Gateway, Foundation Model APIs, Lakebase-backed agent memory and sessions, MCP servers and tools, AI Search, Genie Agents, MLflow tracing and evaluation, and Unity Catalog (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/concepts/)
Agent Runtime is an Agent Bricks component that hosts the agent server at an authenticated endpoint (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/concepts/)

The Agent Bricks docs were rewritten for code-first agents on 2026-10-05, per the October 2026 release-note entry 'Agent Bricks documentation for code-first agent development' (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/october)
The Databricks Agent Bricks CLI has been in Beta since 2026-09-29 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/september)

The Agent Bricks CLI scaffolds custom code agents, runs them locally and deploys them to the Databricks agent runtime, and no workspace preview toggle is needed to use it (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/custom-agents/agent-bricks-cli)
The Agent Bricks CLI is a component of the Agent Bricks agent developer platform (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/concepts/)

For new code agents Databricks recommends the Agent Bricks CLI with DurableAgentServer on Agent Runtime, which runs on Databricks Apps (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/agent-framework/author-agent)
The invocation API for agents on Agent Runtime with DurableAgentServer is `/api/invocations` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/agent-framework/author-agent)

DurableAgentServer supersedes the earlier MLflow AgentServer, adding persistent run state, crash recovery, idempotent invocations and ordered sessions that AgentServer lacks (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/agent-framework/author-agent)

The MLflow AgentServer agent server on Databricks Apps is legacy as of 2026-11-14 and exposes `/responses`, not `/api/invocations` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/agent-framework/author-agent ; https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/legacy/)

For MLflow AgentServer agents on Databricks Apps, app names must start with `agent-` to appear in the workspace Agents list, only medium and large app compute sizes are supported, and the MLflow Review App chat UI does not support agents deployed on Apps (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/agent-framework/author-agent)

Custom agents deployed to Model Serving endpoints are legacy: the deploy page lists 'Model Serving (legacy)' for earlier agents, and no retirement date is published (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/deploy/)

The migration guide from Model Serving to Databricks Apps replaces the `ResponsesAgent` class with module-level `@invoke()` and `@stream()` functions and moves resource declarations from the MLmodel file into `databricks.yml` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/custom-agents/migrate-agent-to-apps)

Databricks still recommends wrapping any framework in the MLflow `ResponsesAgent` interface; supported authoring libraries are LangGraph, LangChain, OpenAI (including the OpenAI Agents SDK) and LlamaIndex (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/agent-framework/author-agent)
LangGraph is one of the two Agent Bricks CLI templates (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/custom-agents/agent-bricks-cli)
The OpenAI Agents SDK is one of the two Agent Bricks CLI templates (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/custom-agents/agent-bricks-cli)

Knowledge Assistant became legacy on 2026-10-12; Databricks recommends the Agent Bricks CLI for code agents and Genie Agents for no-code agents (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/october)
Supervisor Agent became legacy on 2026-10-12 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/october ; https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/legacy/)
The Databricks Supervisor API is deprecated (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/legacy/)
Databricks recommends Genie Agents for no-code agents now that Knowledge Assistant and Supervisor Agent are legacy (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/october)
'Create a custom LLM agent' is legacy, replaced by AI Functions such as `ai_query` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/legacy/)

AI Playground is now listed as a legacy agent offering; Databricks points to the model query docs for querying models and to `agentbricks dev` for building and testing agents (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/legacy/)

facts.fact: Omnigent is Databricks' open-source (Apache 2.0) meta-harness for combining agents, with a Databricks-managed version (secondary) (https://www.databricks.com/blog/introducing-omnigent-meta-harness-combine-control-and-share-your-agents ; https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/omnigent/)
Omnigent coordinates Claude Code, Codex and custom agents defined in YAML (secondary) (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/omnigent/)
Omnigent coordinates Codex alongside Claude Code and custom YAML-defined agents (secondary) (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/omnigent/)

The Omnigent launch blog calls the open-source project alpha, and a Databricks answers page calls the managed version Beta (secondary) (https://www.databricks.com/blog/introducing-omnigent-meta-harness-combine-control-and-share-your-agents ; https://answers.databricks.com/omnigent)
Agent Bricks recommends Omnigent for multi-agent coordination (secondary) (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/omnigent/)

Unity Gateway has been GA since 2026-08-04 as the governance layer for models, MCP servers, agents and skills, though service policies and agent services were still Beta at GA (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/august)
Unity Gateway is built on Unity Catalog (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ai-gateway/)
Unity Gateway doc paths still use `/ai-gateway/` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ai-gateway/)

The product was renamed AI Gateway, then 'Unity AI Gateway', then 'Unity Gateway'; secondary sources date the move into Unity Catalog as Unity AI Gateway to about 2026-04-15, and current docs use 'Unity Gateway' (secondary) (https://kanerika.com/blogs/databricks-unity-ai-gateway/ ; https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/unity-gateway/)
AI Gateway became 'Unity AI Gateway' when it moved into Unity Catalog, dated to about 2026-04-15 by secondary sources (secondary) (https://kanerika.com/blogs/databricks-unity-ai-gateway/)
No official release note was found for the final rename to Unity Gateway (secondary) (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/unity-gateway/)

Unity Gateway has five object types: model service, model provider service, MCP service, skill and service policy; securables are named `catalog.schema.name`, and Databricks-provided services live in `system.ai` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/unity-gateway/concepts)
A Unity Gateway model service routes to one or more models, with traffic splitting and fallbacks (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/unity-gateway/concepts)
A Unity Gateway model provider service is an external provider with centrally managed credentials (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/unity-gateway/concepts)
A Unity Gateway service policy is a guardrail, not a securable (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/unity-gateway/concepts)
MCP service is one of the five Unity Gateway object types (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/unity-gateway/concepts)
In Unity Gateway, `EXECUTE` is needed to call a model service, provider service or MCP service (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/unity-gateway/concepts)
In Unity Gateway, `CREATE SERVICE` is needed to create services in a schema (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/unity-gateway/concepts)
In Unity Gateway, `READ METADATA` is needed to inspect service configuration (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/unity-gateway/concepts)
In Unity Gateway, `MANAGE` is needed to change configuration and grant access (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/unity-gateway/concepts)

facts.fact: Unity Gateway callers also need `USE CATALOG` and `USE SCHEMA` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/unity-gateway/concepts)
Unity Gateway guardrails are service policies, which can be built-in, custom or external (a partner guardrail vendor) (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ai-gateway/)

Beta Unity Gateway policy features include external partner guardrails (2026-10-07), request tags in policies (2026-10-09), a jailbreak guardrail on MCP tool calls and results (2026-10-21) and Python-defined custom service policies (2026-11-11) (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/october ; https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/november)

Unity Catalog Skills entered Beta on 2026-08-28; the Skills API and developer tools entered Beta on 2026-10-12; a GitHub Action that publishes Git-managed skills to Unity Catalog entered Beta on 2026-11-04 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/august ; https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/october ; https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/november)
Skills are one of the Unity Gateway object types governed through Unity Catalog (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/august)

Foundation Model APIs serve frontier models natively as Databricks-hosted `databricks-*` endpoints and `system.ai.*` model services (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/machine-learning/foundation-model-apis/supported-models)

Claude models on Foundation Model APIs include Opus 5.5 (`databricks-claude-opus-5-5`), Opus 5, Opus 4.8-4.1, Sonnet 5.5, Sonnet 5, Sonnet 4.6/4.5, Haiku 5.5, Haiku 4.5, and Fable 5.2, 5.1 and 5 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/machine-learning/foundation-model-apis/supported-models)
Fable 5.2 is hosted by Databricks through Amazon Bedrock and is Unity Gateway-only (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/machine-learning/foundation-model-apis/supported-models)

Hosted OpenAI models include GPT-6.1 Terra (added 2026-10-27), GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Sol, Luna and Astra, GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra and Luna, GPT-5.5 and 5.5 Pro, GPT-5.4 (mini and nano), GPT-5.3 Codex, GPT-5.2, GPT-5.1, GPT-5 (mini and nano), and GPT OSS 120B and 20B (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/machine-learning/foundation-model-apis/supported-models ; https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/october)
Some hosted OpenAI models are not shown in AI Playground (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/machine-learning/foundation-model-apis/supported-models)

Hosted Gemini models include Gemini 4 Hydrogen (Vertex AI-hosted, added 2026-11-12), Gemini 4 Carbon (2026-11-10), Gemini 4 Argon (2026-10-13), Gemini 3.8, 3.7 and 3.5 Flash, Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview, and image models (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/machine-learning/foundation-model-apis/supported-models)
Most hosted Gemini models on Databricks are global endpoints that need cross-geography routing (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/machine-learning/foundation-model-apis/supported-models)
Gemini 3.6 Flash retires on Databricks on 2026-11-19, and its calls redirect to Gemini 3.8 Flash at the same price (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/november)

Other hosted models include xAI Grok 4.7 and 4.6, Zhipu GLM 5.3 and 5.3 Flash, Moonshot Kimi K3 and K3.1 Pro, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (1017), Llama 4 Maverick, Llama 3.3 70B, Llama 3.1 8B, Gemma 3 12B, Qwen3.5 122B and Qwen3-Next 80B (Public Preview), and the OpenJev judge model (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/machine-learning/foundation-model-apis/supported-models)
GLM 5.2 is legacy on Databricks Foundation Model APIs and retires 2027-02-04 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/machine-learning/foundation-model-apis/supported-models)

facts.fact: Foundation models retire on short cycles, so pin to current endpoints: retired in October-November 2026 were Gemini 2.5 Pro and Flash (2026-10-02), Kimi K2.7, Inkling and DeepSeek V4 Pro (2026-10-30), and DeepSeek V4 Flash 0731 (2026-11-05) (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/october ; https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/november)
Gemini 2.5 Pro and Flash retired on Databricks on 2026-10-02 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/october)
DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (non-1017) retires on Databricks on 2026-11-19 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/november)
Claude Sonnet 4 retired on Databricks on 2026-10-09 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/october)

External models are now model provider services in Unity Gateway, covering OpenAI, Anthropic, Gemini and Amazon Bedrock with bring-your-own-key credentials (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ai-gateway/query-model-provider-services)
Unity Gateway model provider services support Amazon Bedrock, including Bedrock Mantle added on 2026-10-09 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/october)

A provider API key can be backed by a Unity Catalog secret (2026-09-21), and a price multiplier reflects negotiated rates (2026-09-19) (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/september)
Databricks recommends provisioned throughput for production foundation model workloads (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/machine-learning/foundation-model-apis/supported-models)
Priority pay-per-token went GA for partner models on 2026-07-22 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/july)
Vector Search was renamed AI Search on 2026-06-01, and the same release added full-text search indexes that need no embeddings (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/june)
Many AI Search APIs and identifiers keep the old Vector Search name, for example REST paths under `/api/2.0/vector-search/...` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/vector-search/vector-search)

AI Search index types are Delta Sync with Databricks-computed embeddings, Delta Sync with self-managed embeddings (cannot later be converted), Direct Vector Access (updated through the REST API), and the full-text index (Beta; BM25; storage-optimized endpoints with triggered sync only) (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/vector-search/vector-search)

AI Search standard endpoints hold about 320M vectors at 768 dimensions and support high QPS (High QPS GA for standard endpoints on 2026-07-15); storage-optimized endpoints hold over 1B vectors, index 10-20x faster and add about 250 ms of query latency (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/vector-search/vector-search ; https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/july)

AI Search storage-optimized endpoints do not support continuous sync, need an embedding dimension divisible by 16, and use a SQL-like filter string (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/vector-search/create-vector-search)

The `ai_search` SQL function can retrieve from Lakebase synced tables (Beta, 2026-09-24), and its `generate_citations` option shows which chunks support each answer (Beta, 2026-09-08) (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/september)
AI Search gained struct and map columns and filter-only queries on 2026-09-02 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/september)
Genie Spaces were renamed Genie Agents on 2026-07-08 with no capability change (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/july)
Genie Agents API paths still use `/api/2.0/genie/spaces/...` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/genie-agents/conversation-api)
Genie One is account-level natural-language analytics grounded in Genie Ontology (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/genie-one/api)
Genie Ontology has been GA since 2026-11-09 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/november)

Databricks Apps is the runtime for Agent Runtime and custom MCP servers (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/databricks-apps/)
Databricks Apps are billed per hour of compute while running (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/databricks-apps/)
Databricks Apps horizontal scaling and OpenTelemetry telemetry to Unity Catalog tables went GA in September 2026 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/september)

Databricks Apps compute sizes are Medium (default; up to 2 vCPU, 6 GB, 0.5 DBU/h), Large (up to 4 vCPU, 12 GB, 1 DBU/h) and XLarge (up to 12 vCPU, 48 GB, 3 DBU/h; region-limited), set by the REST `compute_size` field as `MEDIUM`, `LARGE` or `XLARGE` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/databricks-apps/compute-size)

Databricks Apps run Python 3.11, Node.js 22 and uv 0.13.5 on Ubuntu 22.04 and inject `DATABRICKS_APP_PORT`, `DATABRICKS_APP_URL`, `DATABRICKS_HOST`, `DATABRICKS_APP_NAME`, `DATABRICKS_WORKSPACE_ID`, `DATABRICKS_CLIENT_ID` and `DATABRICKS_CLIENT_SECRET` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/databricks-apps/system-env)
Lakebase, managed Postgres with branching and Unity Catalog synced tables, has been GA since 2026-01-22 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/lakebase/)

Since 2026-03-12 new Lakebase instances are Autoscaling projects (Provisioned instances auto-upgraded since June 2026), and Autoscaling supports Postgres 16, 17 and 18, with 17 the default (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/oltp/ ; https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/lakebase/)

Lakeflow is the data engineering family covering Lakeflow Connect (managed connectors), Lakeflow pipelines, Lakeflow Designer (visual data prep) and Lakeflow Jobs (orchestration) (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/data-engineering/)

Lakeflow pipelines (formerly Delta Live Tables) are built on Apache Spark Declarative Pipelines; old `import dlt` code still works, and `from pyspark import pipelines as dp` is recommended (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ldp/where-is-dlt)

Genie Code tasks in Lakeflow Jobs went GA on 2026-10-21, and AI Function tasks for jobs entered Beta on 2026-11-04 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/october ; https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/november)
Delta Sharing was renamed OpenSharing on 2026-06-10, alongside an open-source OpenSharing release (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/june)

OpenSharing modes are Databricks-to-Databricks (no recipient token; can share notebooks, volumes and Unity Catalog models) and Databricks-to-Open (bearer token or OIDC federation); inviting recipients by email has been Beta since 2026-09-22 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/delta-sharing/)

No Databricks-native computer-use or browser-use agent capability was found in the docs reviewed; the closest offerings are `system.ai.web_search` (Beta) and `system.ai.sandbox` (Beta) (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/generative-ai/mcp/managed-mcp)
`system.ai.web_search` is Beta (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/generative-ai/mcp/managed-mcp)

The Unity Gateway model query base URL is `https://<workspace-url>/ai-gateway/mlflow/v1`, with paths `/responses` (Unified Responses API, OpenResponses-compatible; recommended), `/chat/completions` and `/embeddings`, and the `model` field is a model service name such as `system.ai.claude-sonnet-4-5` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ai-gateway/query-model-services)
Unity Gateway exposes the Unified Responses API at `/ai-gateway/mlflow/v1/responses`, OpenResponses-compatible and recommended (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ai-gateway/query-model-services)
Querying Unity Gateway model services requires the Workspace access or Consumer access entitlement (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ai-gateway/query-model-services)

Native provider paths under Unity Gateway are `/ai-gateway/openai/v1/chat/completions`, `/ai-gateway/openai/v1/responses`, `/ai-gateway/openai/v1/embeddings`, `/ai-gateway/anthropic/v1/messages`, and `/ai-gateway/gemini/v1beta/models/<model>:generateContent` (and `:streamGenerateContent`) (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ai-gateway/query-model-provider-services)

Native provider requests through Unity Gateway carry the `Databricks-Model-Provider-Service: <catalog.schema.service>` header and use a Databricks token, not the provider key (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ai-gateway/query-model-provider-services)

To migrate to Unity Gateway, map `/serving-endpoints` to `/ai-gateway/mlflow/v1`, `databricks-<model>` endpoint names to `system.ai.<model>`, `ai_query('<endpoint>')` to `ai_query('system.ai.<model>')`, and regional `*.ai-gateway.*` hosts to the workspace `/ai-gateway/` route; custom models and agents still use `/serving-endpoints` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ai-gateway/migrate-to-unity-gateway)
Under Unity Gateway, `ai_query('<endpoint>')` becomes `ai_query('system.ai.<model>')` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ai-gateway/migrate-to-unity-gateway)

facts.fact: Databricks-provided `system.ai` MCPs run through Unity Gateway at `https://<workspace-hostname>/ai-gateway/mcp-services/<mcp-name>` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/generative-ai/mcp/managed-mcp)
Databricks-provided `system.ai` MCPs use the OAuth scope `ai-gateway` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/generative-ai/mcp/managed-mcp)

`system.ai.genie_one_mcp` is GA, while `system.ai.dbsql`, `system.ai.web_search` and `system.ai.sandbox` are Beta and need an account admin to enable the Enhanced Unity Gateway preview (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/generative-ai/mcp/managed-mcp)

External-service MCPs in `system.ai` are `system.ai.slack`, `system.ai.github` (public repos only by default), `system.ai.atlassian`, `system.ai.asana`, `system.ai.google_drive`, `system.ai.google_calendar`, `system.ai.gmail` and `system.ai.microsoft_365`, using per-user provider sign-in on first use (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/generative-ai/mcp/managed-mcp)
No GA or preview status is stated for the external-service `system.ai` MCPs (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/generative-ai/mcp/managed-mcp)

Workspace managed MCP endpoints are Public Preview and bypass Unity Gateway governance: they get no Unity Gateway tracing, MCP grants, policies or guardrails (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/generative-ai/mcp/managed-mcp)
A workspace admin must enable the Managed MCP Servers preview before workspace managed MCP endpoints can be used (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/generative-ai/mcp/managed-mcp)

Workspace managed MCP endpoints are Genie Agent `https://<host>/api/2.0/mcp/genie/{genie_space_id}` (scope `genie`), AI Search `https://<host>/api/2.0/mcp/ai-search/{catalog}/{schema}/{index_name}` (scope `ai-search`), DBSQL legacy `https://<host>/api/2.0/mcp/sql` (scope `sql`) and UC functions `https://<host>/api/2.0/mcp/functions/{catalog}/{schema}/{function_name}` (scope `unity-catalog`) (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/generative-ai/mcp/managed-mcp)

The Genie One MCP server URL is `https://<workspace-hostname>/ai-gateway/mcp-services/system.ai.genie_one_mcp?o=<workspace-id>` over Streamable HTTP, with tools `genie_ask`, `genie_poll_response`, `genie_get_query_result`, `genie_cancel_response` and `view_ask` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/mcp-tools/genie-mcp)
The Genie One MCP server accepts OAuth U2M, OAuth M2M or a PAT as a bearer token, and on-behalf-of OAuth needs the `ai-gateway` scope (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/mcp-tools/genie-mcp)
The Genie One MCP server accepts a PAT as a bearer token (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/mcp-tools/genie-mcp)
Genie One MCP callers need `EXECUTE` on `system.ai.genie_one_mcp`, `USE CATALOG` on `system` and `USE SCHEMA` on `system.ai` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/mcp-tools/genie-mcp)

The old Genie MCP Beta endpoint `/api/2.0/mcp/genie` is being sunset with conflicting dates: the 2026-09-25 release note says 2026-10-31, and the newer Genie One MCP page says end of life is 2026-11-30, after which requests fail (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/september ; https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/mcp-tools/genie-mcp)

To migrate from `/api/2.0/mcp/genie` to the Genie One MCP server, change the URL and request the `ai-gateway` scope instead of `genie`; tool names do not change (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/mcp-tools/genie-mcp)

The `system.ai.dbsql` MCP (Beta) is at `https://<host>/ai-gateway/mcp-services/system.ai.dbsql` with the `ai-gateway` scope and the tool `execute_sql`; pass `warehouse_id` in `_meta` to choose a warehouse (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/mcp-tools/databricks-sql)

The `system.ai.dbsql` MCP runs arbitrary SQL as the caller and allows writes by default; set `disallow_writes: true` in the `system.ai.dbsql_policy` policy to make it read-only, and queries are asynchronous and need polling (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/mcp-tools/databricks-sql)

External MCP servers are registered as Unity Gateway MCP services backed by a Unity Catalog HTTP connection, via Unity Gateway > MCPs > + MCP > Connect an existing MCP server or the API at `/api/2.1/unity-catalog/mcp-services`; clients then call `https://<workspace-hostname>/ai-gateway/mcp-services/<catalog>.<schema>.<service>` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ai-gateway/register-mcp-service)
A registered external MCP server must support Streamable HTTP (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ai-gateway/register-mcp-service)
Registering an external MCP service needs `CREATE SERVICE` on the schema and `CREATE CONNECTION` or `USE CONNECTION` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ai-gateway/register-mcp-service)

Unity Catalog HTTP connection auth types are Bearer token, OAuth M2M (recommended), OAuth U2M Shared, OAuth U2M Per User, Dynamic Client Registration (RFC 7591), and Databricks-managed OAuth providers (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/query-federation/http)
Schema-level Unity Catalog HTTP connections are GA, and metastore-level ones are Public Preview (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/query-federation/http)

A bring-your-own OAuth app for a Unity Catalog HTTP connection needs the redirect URL `https://<workspace-hostname>/login/oauth/http.html` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ai-gateway/register-mcp-service)

Agents can call plain REST APIs through the Unity Catalog connection proxy at `https://<workspace-hostname>/api/2.0/unity-catalog/connections/<connection-name>/proxy[/<sub-path>]`, which needs `USE CONNECTION` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/query-federation/http)
The `http_request` SQL function is deprecated and blocked for the U2M Per User and DCR connection types (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/query-federation/http)

Custom MCP servers can be hosted on Databricks Apps; name the app with an `mcp-` prefix so AI Playground recognizes it, use Streamable HTTP, listen on `0.0.0.0:$DATABRICKS_APP_PORT` (default 8000), and template apps serve at `https://<app-hostname>/mcp` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/mcp-tools/custom-mcp)

Callers of a custom MCP server on Databricks Apps need `CAN USE` on the app and an OAuth token; personal access tokens are not supported (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/mcp-tools/custom-mcp)

facts.fact: Default OAuth apps for ChatGPT, Codex, Claude, Claude Code and Cursor went GA on 2026-10-27, so external agents can connect to Databricks MCP servers without a custom OAuth app (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/october)
Context-based ingress policies can allow ChatGPT and Claude traffic as partner platforms (2026-11-10) (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/november)
With app authorization, an agent on Databricks Apps runs as the app's service principal (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/custom-agents/agent-authentication)

User authorization (on-behalf-of user, Public Preview) forwards a downscoped user token in `x-forwarded-access-token`, with scopes such as `user_api_scopes: [sql, genie, model-serving]` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/custom-agents/agent-authentication)
Call `get_user_workspace_client()` inside `invoke` or `stream`, not at startup (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/custom-agents/agent-authentication)

Genie Agents Conversation API paths are `POST /api/2.0/genie/spaces/{space_id}/start-conversation`, `POST .../conversations/{conversation_id}/messages`, `GET .../messages/{message_id}`, `GET .../attachments/{attachment_id}/query-result` and `POST .../attachments/{attachment_id}/execute-query` (https://docs.databricks.com/api/genie/v1/conversation)
Genie Conversation API message, query-result and execute-query operations are labeled GA (https://docs.databricks.com/api/genie/v1/conversation)
Genie Conversation API callers need at least CAN VIEW on the agent and `SELECT` on the data (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/genie-agents/conversation-api)

The Genie One API (Beta) base path is `/api/2.0/genie/one`; `POST /responses` returns an SSE stream, and other endpoints list, get and delete conversations and their items (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/genie-one/api)
The Genie One API needs an OAuth token with the `genie` scope (U2M or M2M) and a workspace admin to enable the Genie One API preview (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/genie-one/api)

SQL Statement Execution API endpoints are `POST /api/2.0/sql/statements/`, `GET /api/2.0/sql/statements/{statement_id}`, `POST .../{statement_id}/cancel` and `GET .../result/chunks/{chunk_index}`, and the caller needs CAN USE on the warehouse (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/sql-execution-tutorial)
`wait_timeout` is 5-50 s (default 10 s; `0s` returns immediately), and `on_wait_timeout` can be `CONTINUE` or `CANCEL` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/sql-execution-tutorial)

A 429 means your own limit was hit (body includes `limit_type`, `limit`, `current` and `retry_after`), while a 503 means Databricks capacity and does not count against your limits, so retry with backoff or use provisioned throughput; requests that set `max_tokens` reserve OTPM up front and can be rejected with a 429 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/machine-learning/foundation-model-apis/limits)

Custom model and agent serving limits: 16 MB payloads (4 MB for agent endpoints), 597 s request timeout, 1,000 endpoints and 200 QPS per workspace without route optimization (300,000 with it), provisioned concurrency 1,024 per endpoint and 4,096 per workspace, and 50 create and update operations per 5 minutes per workspace (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/machine-learning/model-serving/model-serving-limits)

Short bursts can exceed Unity Gateway rate limits because enforcement is per instance (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ai-gateway/rate-limits)

Fixed MCP QPS limits per workspace: managed UC functions, Vector Search and Genie MCP servers allow 50 QPS, managed SQL MCP servers 10 QPS, and external MCP servers 50 QPS (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/resources/limits)

AI Search defaults are 500 endpoints per workspace, 50 indexes per endpoint, embedding dimension up to 4,096, 100 KB Delta Sync row size, 10 MB Direct Vector upsert, 10 MB response, and max results of 10,000 for ANN and full-text but only 200 for hybrid, all adjustable (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/resources/limits)

facts.fact: The Genie One API allows one question per request and one active response per conversation, with questions limited to 25,000 UTF-8 bytes (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/genie-one/api)
A second Genie One question while a response is active returns HTTP 409, and workspace rate limits return HTTP 429 `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/genie-one/api)

The Statement Execution API caps `INLINE` results at 25 MiB and larger results fail the statement; use `EXTERNAL_LINKS` (JSON, CSV or `ARROW_STREAM` chunks through presigned URLs) instead (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/sql-execution-tutorial)

Do not send the Databricks `Authorization` header to Statement Execution API presigned URLs, and only the submitting user can fetch results (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/dev-tools/sql-execution-tutorial)
Each workspace allows 100 Databricks Apps (fixed) (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/resources/limits)

Jobs API limits are 35 RPS for `/jobs/runs/submit`, 20 RPS for `/jobs/run-now` and 100 RPS for `/jobs/runs/get`, with 2,000 concurrent tasks per workspace (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/resources/limits)

Databricks Apps endpoints do not accept PATs; agents and MCP servers on Apps require OAuth tokens, for example from `databricks auth token` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/mcp-tools/custom-mcp)

Missing user-authorization scopes make `get_current_user` fail, and if a diagnostic tool returns a UUID instead of a username, `get_user_workspace_client()` has silently fallen back to the app service principal (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/custom-agents/agent-authentication)

After user authorization is first enabled, existing apps must be restarted, and scope changes take up to 5 minutes to propagate (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/custom-agents/agent-authentication)
In bundles, a resource `name` that doesn't match a `value_from` reference resolves the variable to `None` (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/agents/custom-agents/agent-authentication)

The Enforce Unity Gateway setting disables pay-per-token `databricks-` endpoints and stops traffic to active legacy endpoints; rate limits, budgets, permissions and inference tables do not carry over, so check `system.serving.endpoint_usage` before enforcing (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ai-gateway/migrate-to-unity-gateway)

AI Search endpoints cannot yet be created through Unity Gateway, which breaks Knowledge Assistant and Supervisor agents when Unity Gateway is enforced, and an `ai-gateway`-scoped PAT on the regional host returns 403 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ai-gateway/migrate-to-unity-gateway)
`ai_query` accepts only `system.ai` models; custom model services created in Unity Gateway are not supported yet (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ai-gateway/query-model-services)

`system.ai.web_search` is unavailable in HIPAA/BAA workspaces; `web_search` and `sandbox` are unavailable to consumer-access-only users; sandbox egress isn't guaranteed; Slack, Google and Microsoft 365 connectors need client-side admin app approval or consent; GitHub private repos need the Databricks GitHub connector app (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/generative-ai/mcp/managed-mcp)

Managed MCP connectors, including those for Genie One and Genie Code, moved under Unity Gateway on 2026-08-06, and users had to reconnect them (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/august)

Lakebase OAuth credentials expire after one hour; open connections survive expiry but commands that need authentication fail, so refresh tokens in the connection pool (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/oltp/projects/authentication)

On AWS, Model Serving, Unity Gateway, AI Search and Lakebase are not available in ap-southeast-3, eu-west-3 or us-west-1; Unity Gateway, AI Search, Lakebase and Sandbox are not in us-gov-west-1; Lakebase is also not in ap-northeast-2; pay-per-token needs cross-geo routing in ap-northeast-2, ap-south-1, ap-southeast-1 and ap-southeast-2; MCP servers and UC HTTP connections follow Custom Model Serving regions (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/resources/feature-region-support)

On GCP, Model Serving, Unity Gateway and AI Search cover 8 regions (asia-south1, asia-southeast1, europe-west2, europe-west3, us-central1, us-east1, us-east4, us-west1); pay-per-token works natively in the 4 US regions and needs cross-geo routing in the Asian and European ones; Lakebase and Sandbox are not listed on the GCP page (https://docs.databricks.com/gcp/en/resources/feature-region-support)

On Azure, Government regions (`usgovaz`, `usgovva`) support none of the limited features, nor Databricks SQL or Unity Catalog, and many regions need cross-geo routing for pay-per-token and Knowledge Assistant (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/resources/feature-region-support)

Custom Model Serving is not enabled for Azure `uksouth` workspaces created after 2026-04-30, and Gemini 4 Argon is provided on Azure as an ADI service (https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/databricks/resources/feature-region-support ; https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/machine-learning/foundation-model-apis/supported-models)

facts.fact: Unused service principal OAuth secrets are deleted after 90 days (since 2026-09-16) (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/september)
Maintenance windows are posted on the status page; for example, 2026-11-15 had Databricks SQL us-east-2 from 05:00 to 06:00 UTC and us-west-2 from 06:00 to 07:00 UTC (https://status.databricks.com/)
Continuous Lakeflow pipelines can limit restart-requiring updates to a chosen weekly one-hour window (2026-09-10) (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/2026/september)

Recent renames: Databricks Asset Bundles became Declarative Automation Bundles (2026-03-16), Vector Search became AI Search (2026-06-01), Delta Sharing became OpenSharing (2026-06-10), Genie Spaces became Genie Agents (2026-07-08), AI Gateway became Unity AI Gateway and then Unity Gateway (about 2026-04, secondary), and Delta Live Tables became Lakeflow pipelines (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/ ; https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/dev-tools/bundles ; https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/ldp/where-is-dlt)

The `serverless_gpu` package was replaced by the Databricks AI Runtime SDK on 2026-10-13 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/product/)

Unconfirmed: no official release note was found for the exact date and wording of the final rename from AI Gateway (or Unity AI Gateway) to Unity Gateway; only secondary sources date the Unity AI Gateway step to about April 2026 (https://docs.databricks.com/aws/en/release-notes/unity-gateway/)
